summary: Formalize a PTX implementation of a 1024-input, 3072-output dense ReLU layer and relate its stored output to an upstream TorchLean nn.Sequential specification with explicit weights and bias.
Cover one forward layer for one input vector, with the PTX instruction forms, machine state, and execution rules required by its kernel.
Execute the concatenated four-block kernel per thread through return, store its ordered row result and preserve every other memory word.
Specialize execution to concrete FloatLib binary32 addition and FMA with a reference-arithmetic result.
Decode finite preactivations and prove exact real ReLU with preservation of absolute-error bounds.
Bound the finite ordered FMA and bias-addition error by accumulated local half-ULP terms; ReLU preserves this bound on the stored row result.
Connect the finite stored kernel result directly to the real-valued upstream nn.Sequential forward coordinate on decoded inputs, using the existing rounding budget.
remaining: The per-thread modeled kernel is connected to the actual real-valued TorchLean Sequential forward coordinate on decoded inputs, under the existing memory and finite-row contracts and accumulated rounding budget. PTX arithmetic adequacy, CUDA memory refinement, concurrent GPU execution and hardware correspondence remain unproved.
